videos.script: Lesson 1 said a series is several movements added together. This lesson takes them apart. {{apart}} The tool is older than computers. Replace each day with the average of the days around it. {{average}} Average seven days, and every week is in there once. The Monday peak and the Saturday dip cancel. What is left is the level. {{seven}} Do the same with a year of weeks, and the seasons cancel too. That gives the trend. {{trend}} Divide the series by the trend, and what remains is season and noise. Average each week of the year across years, and the season is what repeats. {{season}} Whatever is left after that is the residual. And the residual is where the interesting things hide: holidays that moved, a price that changed, a week the model did not expect. {{residual}} By the end of this lesson you will have taken Panela's three years apart in four lines of Python, and you will know which of the pieces to trust. {{end}}
